title: SEBI Modifies Asset Allocation Rules for Multi-Cap Funds
author: TMFS Compliance
excerpt: SEBI has updated the minimum allocation limits across Large, Mid, and Small cap stocks for Multi-Cap mutual funds.
content: To ensure true-to-label categorization, SEBI has mandated that all multi-cap funds must maintain a minimum of 25% allocation each in Large-cap, Mid-cap, and Small-cap stocks at all times.

title: Understanding the New Capital Gains Tax Rules 2026
author: TMFS Advisory
excerpt: A complete breakdown of the latest changes to Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and Short Term Capital Gains (STCG) on mutual funds.
content:
The recent budget has introduced significant changes to how mutual funds are taxed. Here is what you need to know:

Equity Funds

STCG is now taxed at 20% (up from 15%). LTCG remains at 12.5% but the exemption limit has increased to ₹1.25 Lakh.

Debt Funds

Debt funds continue to be taxed at your marginal income tax slab rate.

title: The Magic of Compounding: Why Starting Early Matters
author: Tirumala Talabaktula
excerpt: Learn how starting your SIP just 5 years earlier can double your retirement corpus.
content:
Albert Einstein famously called compound interest the eighth wonder of the world. In mutual funds, time in the market is vastly more important than timing the market.

Consider this: An investor starting a ₹5,000 SIP at age 25 will accumulate significantly more by age 60 than someone starting a ₹10,000 SIP at age 35, assuming the same 12% return.
